title: One step of gradient descent
starter:
%x  = buffer 8 dtype=f32 slot=0
%y  = buffer 4 dtype=f32 slot=1
%w  = buffer 2 dtype=f32 slot=2
# X is 4x2 (slot 0), y has 4 targets (slot 1), w has 2 weights (slot 2).
# loss = 0.25 * the sum of (X @ w - y)^2. Update w in place: w - 0.1 * d(loss)/dw.
%vx = load %x
%X  = reshape %vx shape=[4 2]
%vw = load %w
%W  = reshape %vw shape=[2 1]
%p  = matmul %X %W
%pf = reshape %p shape=[4]
%vy = load %y
%d  = sub %pf %vy
%sq = mul %d %d
%s  = reduce %sq op=add
%l  = mul %s 0.25
%g  = gradient %l %vw
%lr = expand 0.1 shape=[2]
%st = mul %g %lr
%w1 = add %vw %st
%sw = store %w %w1
%wv = after %w %sw

hints: The starter adds the step instead of subtracting it, so the loss goes up.
Gradient descent moves against the gradient: `w - lr · g`. `sub %vw %st` does it.
The second sample is already a perfect fit (the targets are exactly X @ w), so its gradient is zero and w comes back unchanged. If your answer moves it, the sign or the loss is off.

answer.code:
%x  = buffer 8 dtype=f32 slot=0
%y  = buffer 4 dtype=f32 slot=1
%w  = buffer 2 dtype=f32 slot=2
%vx = load %x
%X  = reshape %vx shape=[4 2]
%vw = load %w
%W  = reshape %vw shape=[2 1]
%p  = matmul %X %W
%pf = reshape %p shape=[4]
%vy = load %y
%d  = sub %pf %vy
%sq = mul %d %d
%s  = reduce %sq op=add
%l  = mul %s 0.25
%g  = gradient %l %vw
%lr = expand 0.1 shape=[2]
%st = mul %g %lr
%w1 = sub %vw %st
%sw = store %w %w1
%wv = after %w %sw
answer.explain: The gradient points uphill, so a step against it lowers the loss. The update reads the old `w` (through `%vw`) and stores into the same buffer, which is safe: a store's value is computed from the contents before the store. A renderer that turns that store into an element-by-element loop has to keep it safe too, by computing the new values first. The lab's MNIST program is this step 50 times, with a bigger model and a softmax loss.
